purpose: Primary open-source numerical quality-threshold research for Loot Liquidator; evidence export, not a universal output-count multiplier.

retrieval.method: Pinned shallow git clones over the configured proxy; files inspected directly with line numbers. No WoW client or server experiment performed.

inputs.S: Effective skill: API baseSkill + bonusSkill, with separately modeled simulation modifiers
inputs.D: Recipe difficulty for the exact recipe and allocation

optionalBreakpointOffset.caveat: CraftSim exposes a one-skill breakpoint workaround. Default is false; it is not proof of a universal +1 game requirement.

sources.support: Implements the numerical quality thresholds for recipes with one, two, three and five qualities.
Counts crossed skill thresholds to select expected output quality; quantity is computed separately.
Reads effective skill as baseSkill plus bonusSkill from operation info, and recipeDifficulty from baseDifficulty.
The quality breakpoint offset option defaults to false.

limits: Open-source implementation is direct evidence of the addon model, not independent in-game validation for every randomized processing recipe.
A piecewise quality selector is not E(quantity) increasing linearly with skill.
Do not carry this modern deterministic quality model backward into historical Dragonflight Inspiration/hidden-skill-variance studies without explicit era proof.
For modified difficulty, prefer actual operation thresholds over assuming CraftSim baseDifficulty alone covers every optional reagent or target.

findings.caveat: upperSkillTreshold is the API field spelling. An arbitrary changed simulated skill cannot be sent into this API; capture real operation thresholds then apply a scoped research model to a simulated target.

sources.support: Generated Blizzard contract exposes skill, difficulty, output quality and current bracketing thresholds.
Blizzard UI uses upperSkillTreshold to show the skill requirement for the next recipe quality.

findings.implementation: For a confirmed two-quality operation without concentration, capture exact current target input, current quality and its boundary. Prefer API bracketing threshold to a universal hardcoded number; validate boundary against current craftingQuality and effective skill.

findings.observedActionHookContract: CraftSalvage(recipeSpellID, numCasts, itemTarget, craftingReagents, applyConcentration); record its actual itemTarget GUID through a secure posthook and do not invoke crafting actions.

sources.support: Generated current API documentation establishes the CraftSalvage argument order and identifies itemTarget as a required ItemLocation.
The normal crafting details path passes the transaction reagent allocation and allocation GUID to operation info.
For salvage transactions, the allocation GUID is the actual salvage item GUID.
CraftSim also resolves the selected salvage input to its inventory item GUID.

implementation: Key a live salvage operation cache by exact recipe plus input item ID/rank and target allocation identity; invalidate on gear, talents, buffs, skill and allocation changes.
Do not reuse a recipe-only operation response with no allocationItemGUID to claim ore/herb-rank-specific requirements.
No target in inventory or no usable response means no live numeric quality claim; retain a source-labeled reference estimate.
Offline character and hypothetical stats must use that character's compatible captured context or an explicit compiled research rule, never current-character operation data.

sources.support: CraftingRecipeOutputInfo returns a representative item identifier/hyperlink/icon; it does not enumerate stochastic cooutput probabilities or quantity distributions.
Recipe schematic has declared minimum/maximum quantity and an operation-info capability flag, rather than per-cooutput skill-conditioned empirical yields.
Expected craft quantity is baseItemAmount plus expected extra Multicraft items, while skill chooses output quality separately.

limits: Do not take the schematic midpoint as a measured random processing mean.
Applying an operation quality to every random gem or byproduct requires recipe/family-specific research or observed outcomes.
This code search did not find a validated universal current milling/prospecting/disenchanting quantity-versus-skill curve.

scope: client build or compatible build interval
recommendedPipelineContract.formulaForTwoRanks: Q=1 if S<T else 2; T is the exact captured or sourced boundary, not a global 365/505 constant.
recommendedPipelineContract.amountPolicy: Keep E_total for an eligible output family unchanged and allocate that family expectation to the selected rank only when deterministic rank allocation is supported. Do not lift unknown/locked conditional expectations.
recommendedPipelineContract.sourcePolicy: Keep source totals, sample counts and confidence separate from quality-rule evidence. Export numerical thresholds/rank maps through the research compiler rather than hand-editing generated ItemDB.
recommendedPipelineContract.rankMapWarning: database/research/rank-families.json states its ids arrays are unordered sets; Crystalline Glass rank order is explicitly disputed. Never index material.rankIDs by numeric quality without verifiedRanks or validated game rank metadata.
recommendedPipelineContract.confidencePolicy: A source-code model does not justify an invented 90% or 100% experimental confidence. Record model evidence and its applicability limits separately.
unresolved: Exact live Midnight input-rank-specific thresholds must come from a current operation capture or a numerically explicit study.
The code model does not establish extra gem/pigment talent proc rates or their interaction with skill.
Disenchanting is not automatically an ordinary deterministic quality-crafting recipe.
